question_text: A 55-year-old woman with diabetes presents to the emergency department due to swelling of her left leg, fever, and chills for the past 2 days. The woman’s maximum recorded temperature at home was 38.3°C (101.0°F). Her left leg is red and swollen from her ankle to the calf, with an ill-defined edge. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 120/78 mm Hg, pulse rate 94/min, temperature 38.3°C (101.0°F), and respiratory rate 16/min. On physical examination, her left leg shows marked tenderness and warmth compared with her right leg. The left inguinal lymph node is enlarged to 3 x 3 cm. Which of the following chemical mediators is the most likely cause of the woman’s fever?
